releases.author: LordNeoZ
releases.description:
Fixes the settings import.

Importing from Periodic Notes or core Daily Notes used to fill every period with defaults. A user with monthly, quarterly or yearly notes configured would lose the folder and have the period switched off — for periods the older plugins never supported in the first place.

Import now only touches periods that actually exist in the legacy configuration and leaves everything else untouched. Covered by two regression tests (39 in total).

Manual installation: download main.js, manifest.json and styles.css into <your vault>/.obsidian/plugins/period-calendar/

releases.author: LordNeoZ
releases.description:
First release.

A calendar for Obsidian where **every period is clickable** — day, week, month, quarter and year — with ISO weeks handled correctly.

### What it does

- **Five clickable periods.** Click a day, a week number, the month name, the year, or the quarter button to open or create that note.
- **Format validation as you type.** The settings screen checks your filename formats and explains what is wrong in plain language, with a one-click fix.
- **Correct ISO weeks.** `YYYY` is the calendar year and does not belong next to `WW`, the ISO week. On 2024-12-30 they disagree — that date is in ISO week 1 of *2025*, so `YYYY-[W]WW` writes `2024-W01` and collides with January. Period Calendar catches this and offers `GGGG-[W]WW` instead.
- **ISO or locale weeks**, with a configurable first day of the week.
- **Subfolders in the format.** `YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD` creates the folder tree for you.
- **Imports your existing setup** from Periodic Notes or core Daily Notes, so migrating moves nothing and orphans no note.
- **Strict filename parsing**, so a note called `Meeting notes` is never mistaken for a date.
- Commands for every period, including opening the calendar view itself and jumping to the next or previous one.

### Installing manually

Download `main.js`, `manifest.json` and `styles.css` into `<your vault>/.obsidian/plugins/period-calendar/`, then enable it under Settings → Community plugins.

### Notes

The period logic has no Obsidian dependencies and is covered by 37 unit tests spanning year boundaries, both week systems, leap years, subfolder paths and legacy import.
